title: The seam: components/ and the first extraction
summary: Create heca/src/components/, fix the contract and the test pattern, and prove both on the highest-frequency composition — the chrome action button.
description:
The folder plus the two rules that decide everything after it, proven on one real extraction rather than asserted in a doc.

## What exists — updated 2026-08-12

**`heca/src/components/mod.rs` EXISTS** (T373, done): the contract and the headless-test pattern, written as the module doc. `mod components;` is in `heca/src/main.rs`. Nothing has moved into it yet.

Everything else is still inline: `heca/src/chrome/mod.rs` (5270 lines), `heca/src/providers/workspaces/mod.rs` (2200), `heca/src/chrome/expose.rs` (2028).

The **chrome action button** is the highest-frequency inline composition and the subject of T374, because AGENTS already documents it as a recipe every caller repeats by hand (AGENTS § "Chrome buttons → action, tooltip, KeyHint"):

1. `action_tooltip(button, action_name, label, &state.action_shortcuts)` — `heca/src/chrome/mod.rs:633` — composes `"<label>  <shortcut>"` from the action's **name**.
2. `KeyHint::new(w).on_peek(fires(intent, emit))` for the pick + `.on_click(move || emit(…))` for the click — one declaration each, via `chrome::fires()` :3040. **A pick is not a click**: they are different gestures and a region may answer them differently, so the two closures are deliberately separate and only collapse when the act genuinely is the same (a header button).

⚠️ **This phase used to describe step 2 as `hints.register(InteractionIntent::…)` + `.hint_target(id)`. That API is DELETED** — `HintTargetRegistry`, `HintTargets`, `HintTargetId`, `Base::hint_target` and `named_press` were all removed by F004/P084/T399 under ⭐⭐ RULE ZERO, because a plugin could construct none of them. Do not reintroduce any of them, and do not "preserve" hint-id monotonicity: nothing is registered any more, so nothing has to be un-registered when a tree rebuilds. The framework collects the declarations out of the laid-out tree (`heca_grid_ui::collect_peeks`) and runs one (`fire_peek`).

Call sites doing the recipe by hand: `build_pane_header()` :860 (per configured `PaneAction`, via `pane_action_spec()` :652), `sidebar_toggle_button()` :1834, and the overlay's action buttons (`heca/src/chrome/overlay.rs:560`, which already funnels through `action_tooltip`).

## The contract fixed here (T373, landed)

- A component takes **plain data plus the app seams it binds** — `Intent` / `ChromeIntentEmitter`, `&mut BuildCx` (drag, signals), an action **name**, a theme. **Never `&AppState`**: it needs a window, so a component that takes it is a component nobody can test. Same split that made `route_in_domain`, `cursor_follow` and `resolve_context_for` testable.
- A component **never** spells a shortcut, picks a glyph, or hardcodes a measure. Name the action; the catalog and `ActionShortcuts` answer.
- **Sizes are shares, never computed pixels** — `Length::Pct` of a shared denominator, or a `grow` weight. A composition that multiplies model numbers by a scale of its own has taken over the layout engine's job and then owns every term (the exposé's seven attempts).
- **Where it lives**: beside its surface (`heca/src/chrome/<surface>/`) until a **second** surface wants it; the second caller is the move. `heca/src/components/` is the home for the shared case.
- If a proposed component binds **no** app concept, it is a widget in the wrong crate — send it to `heca-grid-ui` instead.

## Test pattern established (T373)

Headless, asserting the built tree or the painted scene — not a flag. Follow `heca/src/providers/mod.rs::the_shared_context_carries_nothing_of_one_components_domain` (builds through `ChromeCtx::for_build`, asserts children and what the host registries received) and `heca-grid-ui/tests/phase_a.rs` (paint into a `Scene`, assert `DrawCommand`s). A component sized by shares also gets the test shares exist for: lay it out in a box and assert it never exceeds it.

For the action button (T374), assert: the tooltip carries the action's live shortcut, and the click and the pick carry the **same** intent when — and only when — they are the same act.

## Behaviors to preserve

Identical pixels; identical tooltip text; the existing `pane_action_spec` mapping of `PaneAction` → (glyph, action, label, focus-first) stays the single source of what a header button is.

tasks.title: The chrome action button becomes a component — one call, not a two-step recipe
tasks.description:
The first extraction of the chrome action button — the composition the app repeats most, and the one AGENTS already has to explain step by step.

⚠️ DESCRIPTION CORRECTED 2026-08-24 against the code. Everything below is verified; the previous text described a deleted API, the wrong file, and a premise that is no longer true. What changed is recorded at the bottom so nobody re-derives it.

## What exists — verified 2026-08-24

**`heca/src/components/` is NOT empty.** It holds `folder_line.rs` and `pane_name.rs` alongside `mod.rs`. The feature and phase text saying "nothing has moved into it yet" is stale; the contract and the headless-test pattern in `mod.rs` have live users to read.

**The two-step recipe every caller still performs by hand** (AGENTS § "Chrome buttons → action, tooltip, KeyHint"):

1. `action_tooltip(button, action_name, label, &state.action_shortcuts)` — **`heca/src/chrome/pane_header.rs:451`**, not chrome/mod.rs. Composes `"<label>  <shortcut>"` from the action's **name**, resolving through `ActionShortcuts` so a rebind updates every tip.
2. The click and the pick, declared separately:
       let fire = chrome::fires(intent, emit);              // chrome/mod.rs:1417
       let hint = chrome::picks(mount, intent, emit);        // chrome/mod.rs:1441
       KeyHint::new(button.on_click(fire)).on_hint(hint)
   **A pick is not a click** — they are different gestures and a region may answer them differently; the two collapse only when the act genuinely is the same, which for a header button it is.

**Call sites doing this by hand, verified:**
- `build_pane_header()` — `heca/src/chrome/pane_header.rs:697`, per configured `PaneAction` via `pane_action_spec()` at `pane_header.rs:489`.
- `sidebar_toggle_button()` — `heca/src/chrome/mod.rs:827` (the AGENTS-cited complete example).
- the overlay's dialog buttons — `heca/src/chrome/overlay.rs:559`, which already funnels through `action_tooltip`.

`pane_action_spec` also returns **`needs_focus`**: an active-targeted button (zoom/float — the `WmAction` carries no pane id) must emit a `FocusPane` before its action, while pane-parameterized ones (close/move/split, which carry the pane) just activate. The events are queued and processed in order, so the focus lands on this pane first. The component has to carry that distinction, not flatten it.

## What to build

An action-button component taking: the action **name**, the `Intent` it fires, a label, an optional explicit glyph (default: `ActionCatalog::icon(name)`), a `WidgetSize`, and the seams (`&ActionShortcuts`, the emitter, the mount for `picks`). It returns the tooltip-wrapped, hint-declaring, click-wired button as one value.

Then **delete the hand-wiring at all three call sites in this same task** — an extraction that leaves the recipe behind has achieved nothing and is two sources of truth.

**Where it lives:** `heca/src/components/`, not beside a surface. The location rule says a component moves there on the SECOND caller; this one has three on day one (pane header, sidebar toggle, overlay), so it is born shared.

## Test (headless, asserts the visible thing)

- The tooltip text carries the action's **live** shortcut from `ActionShortcuts`, and is the label alone when unbound.
- The click and the pick carry the **same** intent when — and only when — they are the same act.
- With `needs_focus`, a `FocusPane` is emitted before the action.
- The glyph comes from `ActionCatalog::icon(name)` when none is passed.

## Behaviors to preserve

- **Pixel-identical buttons** — Antonio verifies by eye, and green tests found none of this phase's earlier failures.
- `pane_action_spec` stays the single source of what a header button is.
- The config's `[pane] title_actions` (and any future plugin-added button) keeps flowing through the same dynamic vector — never a per-action `match` in the build loop.
- A component never spells a shortcut or picks a glyph itself: name the action, and the catalog plus `ActionShortcuts` answer.

## What was corrected on 2026-08-24, and why

The previous description said step 2 was `let hint_id = hints.register(InteractionIntent::…)` then `.hint_target(hint_id)`, tested "a hint target was registered", and listed "hint ids stay monotonic and their ranges are removed when a tree rebuilds (`HintTargetRegistry::remove_range`)" as a behaviour to preserve.

**That API is deleted.** `HintTargetRegistry`, `HintTargets`, `HintTargetId`, `Base::hint_target` and `named_press` were removed by F004/P084/T399 under ⭐⭐ RULE ZERO, because a plugin could construct none of them. Grepped 2026-08-24: none of those names exists in heca/src or heca-grid-ui/src. Nothing is registered any more, so there is no monotonicity and no un-registration to preserve — the framework collects declarations out of the laid-out tree (`heca_grid_ui::collect_hints`, hint/collect.rs:101) and runs one (`fire_hint`, hint/fire.rs:20).

The phase text carries this warning already but spells the API `on_peek` / `collect_peeks` / `fire_peek`. The live names are **`on_hint`** (builders.rs:809), **`collect_hints`**, **`fire_hint`** — peek was renamed to hint.

Also corrected: `action_tooltip`, `pane_action_spec` and `build_pane_header` live in `heca/src/chrome/pane_header.rs`, not `chrome/mod.rs`; every line number in the old text pointed at the wrong file. And `heca/src/chrome/expose.rs` is no longer one 2028-line file — it is the `chrome/expose/` folder (T420 landed), so the feature's "current state" section overstates what is left inline. Current sizes: chrome/mod.rs 3265 lines (not 5270), providers/workspaces/mod.rs 1703 (not 2200).

---
**Completion summary:**
Closed 2026-11-18 (Antonio) with NO code change; main is unchanged. An ActionButton component was built and then rejected in design review: the widget library must not be tied to heca's actions; the established form is `.on_click(|ev| ev.dispatch(Intent::new(..)))` (docs/widgets.md:3090, heca-grid-ui/src/event/handlers.rs:47-65), tooltip via `.tooltip(text)` or `action_tooltip` (heca/src/chrome/panes/pane_header/shortcuts.rs:148), `prefix+/` picks automatic. Converting the 3 chrome-button sites (scene/mod.rs sidebar toggle, pane_header/build.rs, overlay/modal.rs) to that form loses behaviour today, verified with temporary tests: Button/IconButton have their own `on_click(Fn())` (button/builders.rs:199, icon_button.rs:127) separate from EventExt::on_click; with only the event form Enter/activate() and the ButtonGroup ⋮ overflow row (button_group.rs:187) do nothing and IconButton stops being focusable; a hint can carry only a closure (intent::dispatch is pub(crate), heca-grid-ui/src/intent.rs:29) so the policy filter on picks is lost; SubmitOverlay{overlay: Some(id)} cannot be expressed as an Intent (input/action.rs:604-611, input/build/chrome.rs:82-85). All of this moved to P087(F011)/T565 (library fix first, then the sites). The rejected attempt is saved as scratchpad t374-v1.patch.

Forced completion overrode 6 unchecked checklist item(s): component takes an action NAME + intent + label + optional glyph + the seams, icon defaults to ActionCatalog::icon(name); shortcut from ActionShortcuts; tooltip via the one composer, hint target and on_click carry the SAME intent; needs_focus emits the focus-then-act composite, every hand-wired call site converted and deleted (build_pane_header, sidebar_toggle_button, overlay buttons), headless test: tooltip shortcut, hint/click intent identity, focus-first variant, catalog glyph, AGENTS recipe section rewritten to 'use the component' (the steps stay only as the explanation). Motivation: Closed by Antonio 2026-11-18 without code changes: the ActionButton extraction was rejected in design review (a widget must not be tied to actions; the established form is on_click(|ev| ev.dispatch(Intent))). Converting the 3 sites is blocked by library gaps, moved into P087(F011)/T565 as its first step.

tasks.title: AGENTS.md § How To Structure and Build a Component — the exposé, written up as the pattern
tasks.description:
**Antonio, 2026-08-13:** *"I want you to write a section in AGENTS.md: How To Structure and Build a Component. and describe here what to do (the way you did with Exposé). create a folder under chrome: chrome/the_component and inside it split in smaller reusable component like react. Describe the best practices and pattern to do that."*

# What to write

A new numbered section in `AGENTS.md`, near § 0b (widget vs component) and cross-referenced from it — § 0b says *where* a component lives and *that* it must be one; this says **how to build one**, as a worked recipe someone can follow without having read this session.

The subject is the exposé (F003/P082/T420), which is the first surface built this way and the reference implementation:

```
heca/src/chrome/<surface>/
├── mod.rs            host wiring — the ONLY file that may touch AppState
├── model.rs          the session reduced to plain data
├── <leaf>_card.rs    the smallest piece
├── <group>_card.rs   … composed of the leaf
├── <row>.rs          … composed of the group
└── testing.rs        #[cfg(test)] shared fixtures
```

## The points it must make, each with the exposé as the example

1. **Split by what each piece OWNS, not by size.** `PaneCard` owns what a card *is*; `ColumnCard` owns the vertical share; `WorkspaceRow` owns the horizontal share and the float rects; `ExposeGrid` owns the row share and the cursor. Every question has exactly one owner, which is what makes a wrong answer findable.
2. **Properties are struct fields; the constructor is a struct literal.** `PaneCard { pane_id, name, active, ws_idx, col_idx, next, theme, cb }.build()` — Flutter/SwiftUI named parameters, not an eleven-argument function (`providers/workspaces/pane_card()` is the counter-example, at eleven positional arguments).
3. **The seams travel as ONE group, not as N arguments per level** — `ExposeCallbacks { choose, delete, cursor_to, dismiss, keys }`, built once by `callbacks(emit, keys)` so a test can supply exactly the app's edges and nothing else.
4. **Never `&AppState`** — it needs a window, so a component that takes it cannot be tested. Only `mod.rs` sees it, and its job is to *gather* and hand down.
5. **Return the concrete widget, not `Box<dyn Component>`, when the parent still has to size it.** A box has no builders left; `PaneCard::build -> (Row, GridCell)` is what lets a column give it a share and a row give it a rect.
6. **A component that produces navigable cells returns them beside its widget** — `(Flex, Vec<GridCell>)` — rather than reaching into a registry.
7. **Sizes are shares** (`Length::Pct` of one shared denominator, `grow` weights); the parent sizes the child, never the child itself. Include the gap-vs-padding trap: a gap is added *outside* a percentage width, so air between percentage-sized siblings belongs in their padding, while a gap between `grow` siblings is exact.
8. **One headless test per component**, plus the box test for anything sized by shares: lay it out and assert it never exceeds what it was given.
9. **`testing.rs` holds the fixtures** so each test reads as the thing it asserts.
10. **It moves to `heca/src/components/` on the SECOND caller** — a move, never a copy.

## Also

- Point § 0b at it, and point `heca/src/components/mod.rs`'s module doc at it, so the three do not drift.
- Keep it a recipe, not a rationale essay — the file is already long and this is the part an agent has to be able to follow at speed.

# Verification

Antonio reads it. The test of the section is whether a fresh agent could build a second surface from it without asking.

---
**Completion summary:**
**Written 2026-08-13** — `AGENTS.md` § **0b-bis. HOW TO STRUCTURE AND BUILD A COMPONENT — the recipe, with a worked example**, sitting between § 0b (widget vs component) and § 0c (the event system). Uncommitted on `feat/palette-modes`.

It opens with the folder — *"a surface is a folder, not a function"* — and then eight numbered steps, each with the exposé worked through it:

1. **Split by what each piece OWNS, never by size** — with the exposé's four components as a table of what each owns *and what it owns nothing about*, against the 400-line `map()` that owned every term at once and was wrong seven times.
2. **Properties are struct fields; the constructor is a struct literal** — Flutter/SwiftUI named parameters in Rust's spelling, against `providers/workspaces/pane_card()`'s eleven positional arguments.
3. **The seams travel as ONE group** — `ExposeCallbacks` + `callbacks(emit, keys)`, and why: that function is what a test calls to get the app's edges and nothing else.
4. **Never `&AppState` outside `mod.rs`** — the single rule that decides whether the surface can be checked without photographing the app.
5. **Return the concrete widget when the parent still has to size it** — a box has no builders left, so boxing forces the child to size itself, which is how a component starts computing geometry. Plus: navigable cells come back beside the widget, never through a registry.
6. **Sizes are shares; the parent sizes the child** — with both traps written out: `grow` alone always fills, and a gap is added *outside* a percentage (so air between percentage-sized siblings belongs in their padding), plus the `flex: 1 1 0` idiom written once per surface.
7. **One headless test per component, plus the box test** — `the_whole_map_never_exceeds_the_box_it_is_given` named as the one that would have caught all seven failures; fixtures in `testing.rs`.
8. **It moves to `heca/src/components/` on the second caller.**

Cross-referenced both ways so the three cannot drift: § 0b now ends with a pointer to it, and `heca/src/components/mod.rs`'s module doc names it as the full recipe and marks its own list as the short form.

tasks.title: FolderLine's gap and icon size are raw pixels — make them tokens before they are copied
tasks.description:
**Small, and it matters because the file is shared.** `heca/src/components/folder_line.rs` (new 2026-08-21) carries:

```rust
const GAP: f32 = 6.0;
const ICON: f32 = 12.0;
```

They were moved **verbatim** from `heca/src/providers/workspaces/pane_row.rs`, where the cwd line was written inline, because the extraction had to be a move and not a behaviour change (the sidebar's row and the exposé's card now share the component). But AGENTS.md is explicit: sizes and colours come from tokens — "hardcode nothing … border width, radius, glow" — and this now sits in `components/`, which is the shelf other surfaces copy from. Two callers today, and every future one inherits the literals.

**Build.**
- `GAP` → a `Spacing` token (`Spacing::Xs` is the gap the exposé's cards use); the gap between a glyph and its label is the same idea everywhere.
- `ICON` → derived from the surrounding text rather than fixed: the line already takes `font_scale`, so the glyph should follow it (a metadata line at 0.85 of the body should not carry a body-sized glyph). Check what `Icon::size` expects and whether a theme font size is reachable from the component's `&GuiTheme`.
- The colours are already tokens (`theme.colors.foreground`) — leave them.

**Verification.** This changes how two surfaces look, so it is Antonio's eye, not a test: the sidebar's cwd row and the exposé card's folder line, at more than one font size (`prefix+Shift+r` after changing `[font] size`). A test can only assert that no literal remains.

**Why here.** F011/P087 is where a shape becomes shared; this is the first component that arrived on the shelf carrying numbers from the surface it came from, and the rule is worth enforcing on the way in.

---
**Completion summary:**
Closed 2026-11-17 (Antonio): already done by later work. heca/src/components/folder_line.rs no longer has the raw GAP/ICON pixel constants: the gap is the Spacing token (`.gap(Spacing::Sm)`), the indent is a Spacing field, and the icon follows the WidgetSize variant (`.size(self.size)`). Verified by reading the file on main 2026-11-17.

tasks.title: CommandPalette composes instead of computing — put-and-use, like every other widget
tasks.description:
Antonio, 2026-08-24, after the showcase's palette rendered with empty rows while the app's was correct: "another sign we are not using the widget and component pattern to build things."

THE TARGET — the line an author writes, anywhere, including a plugin:

  let cp = CommandPalette::new().items(...);
  // later, from anywhere:
  button.on_click(move || cp.open());
  // or, bound to a key / reachable over RPC, with no host code:
  CommandPalette::new().items(...).opens_on("palette.open")

Same shape as every other surface. Nothing to wire, nothing to position, no host pass.

WHERE IT IS NOW
- heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/command_palette.rs (1363 lines) — already ONE widget in the library. This is NOT a duplication problem: the app (heca/src/chrome/palette.rs:360) and the showcase (heca-renderer/examples/showcase.rs:319) both call CommandPalette::new(). heca/src/chrome/palette.rs's 758 lines are host wiring (which commands exist, how one dispatches), not a second palette.
- The defect is that the widget COMPUTES ITS OWN GEOMETRY. command_palette.rs:733 writes `child.base_mut().bounds = target` after calling `crate::component::shift_subtree(child, dx, dy)` (:725-733), and it anchors itself against PaintCx::viewport (see :998, :1303 writing `q.base_mut().bounds`). visible_rows (:588) decides how many rows fit by measuring.
- Consequence, observed: a widget that positions itself renders whatever its host's layout pass happens to hand it. The app lays it out inside a definite window and it is correct; the showcase lays it out in its own detached overlay pass (showcase.rs:2737-2741) and the rows came out empty with two labels drawn over the input. It is also why a framework-level rule (max-width: 100%, layout.rs) landed on one host and not the other — see F003/P082/T438.

WHAT IT VIOLATES (Antonio, 2026-08-24, stating the principles he wants applied)
- SRP / Separation of Concerns: one 1363-line widget owns filtering, selection, row composition, layout, placement, panel sizing, keyboard handling and open state. Each of those has a different reason to change.
- Composition over inheritance/bespoke: placement, clipping and scrolling are already widgets in this library, and the palette re-implements all three.
- DRY: Overlay already owns "centred over the page, capped to the viewport, arrives and leaves" (Presence + Animation, open()/hide()/toggle()); ScrollRegion already owns clip + scroll + ensure_visible. The palette is a second implementation of both.

THE SPLIT
1. Rows become a real composition — a column of rows inside a ScrollRegion, laid out by the engine. Delete the manual pass: no shift_subtree, no writing bounds. This is the bulk of the work.
2. Placement moves to Overlay (heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/overlay/): the palette becomes a panel inside one, so "centred, capped, animated in and out" is asked for rather than reimplemented. Its open/close verbs then come from the vocabulary that already exists — open() / hide() / toggle(), the same one F003/P082/T436 gave KeyHintGroup via opens_on(action_name), which is exactly the pseudocode above and already works end to end for the exposé.
3. Scrolling and "keep the selected row visible" become ScrollRegion::ensure_visible instead of visible_rows arithmetic.
4. What legitimately STAYS the widget's own: fuzzy filtering, the match marks, reflowing the selected row's description, cursor movement. That is behaviour, not geometry. Split it further per SRP: the filter should be a pure function over items (testable with no widget at all), separate from the view that renders its result.

EDGE CASES / WHAT MUST NOT REGRESS
- The reflow of the selected row's description IS the selection's visual: the row grows and the rows below slide down (command_palette.rs, and Label::wrap's doc). It changes the label's MEASURE, so it must survive the move to engine-driven layout.
- Keycap rows: one per binding, stacked, in a column reserved across the list.
- [settings] command_palette_size (560/700/1000px, 6/8/12 rows) currently feeds panel_size; under Overlay this becomes the panel's own size, not a row count the widget computes.
- The palette must still hold the keyboard while open and dismiss through [keys.widgets], as every other modal widget does.

WHEN IT IS DONE
- The same picture in the app, the showcase and a plugin's panel, because none of them positions it.
- It falls under the two sweeps added by F003/P082/T438 automatically (nothing paints outside its box; content never renders as nothing), so "the palette paints outside its box" becomes a test failure rather than a screenshot.

tasks.title: Widgets act through ev.dispatch(Intent), not hand-sent events: audit and fix every site
tasks.description:
AGREED PLAN (Antonio, 2026-11-18, after the read-only audit — DOM / SwiftUI / Flutter model, one path):
1. ONE CLICK PATH. Remove `Component::activate()` (heca-grid-ui/src/component/behavior.rs:316) and the private action field + own `on_click(Fn())` of Button, IconButton, BadgeButton, Toast, Choice, RailCell, Item, Row (fields: button/mod.rs:154, icon_button.rs:44, badge_button.rs:39, toast/mod.rs:99, choice.rs:76, rail_cell.rs:43, item.rs:96, row.rs:59), and the Enter/Space arms copied into their capture hooks. Like a browser <button>: Enter/Space on a focused activatable widget makes the framework deliver a real `Click` event to it; programmatic "press" (a dialog's primary button, a plugin, code) = deliver a `Click` event to the widget (el.click()). Everything reaches the widget's `.on_click(|ev| ..)` handlers. The ButtonGroup ⋮ overflow row delivers a Click to the collapsed button. Per-widget flags (focusable, one_click_target, focus_barrier) stay correct without each widget's builder setting them by hand (central hook; NOT on every widget with a handler — pane shell / dock FocusScope must not claim the press).
2. PLUGINS GET EVERY EVENT. A described node binds an Intent to ANY event the native API has, by the same name — click, double_click, right_click, middle_click, pointer_enter, pointer_leave, focus_gained, focus_lost, key, drag…, plus today's press/change/toggle/dismiss/… — via `.on("<event>", Intent)`. ONE table event-name -> EventKind shared by native and described, with a test failing if they drift. Today described supports only press, change, toggle, action, scroll, activate, hint, dismiss, submit, resize, move, enter (heca-view / heca-view-realize). Sugar `.on_press(Intent)` (native, like described) = click dispatches the Intent AND the pick carries the same Intent (Hint::of), so the picker can hide a letter whose action is refused.
3. ORIGIN. The host intent sink (heca/src/app/startup.rs:192-197) stamps every Intent MouseContent; it must know which surface acted. The host records the origin around each tree's event delivery and maps it with the SAME function the picker uses (pick_source, heca/src/chrome/hint/targets.rs:161-198) — one rule for showing a letter and executing. A dialog button's submit resolves its own overlay from that origin (SubmitOverlay overlay id is #[serde(skip)], input/action.rs:604-611).
4. THREE MISSING ACTIONS (with args): scroll a given terminal (today scroll_to_bottom / scroll_to_offset act on the focused one), toggle a given workspace's collapse (today only toggle_current_workspace_collapsed), the exposé cursor on a pane (ExposeCursor has no catalog name).
5. CONVERT THE SITES (step 2 below). Not widgets, out of scope: palette Commands (Fn()), terminal handle commands, closer/dismiss hooks, the sink itself. Watch: focus_pane as a named action is more permissive with an active float than InteractionIntent::FocusPane (route.rs:84-90 vs :166-172) — eye-check.
Doc drift to fix with it: docs/widgets.md:4125 and AGENTS show fires(intent, emit), code is fires(mount, intent, emit) (heca/src/chrome/input/emitter.rs:138); button_group.rs:17 and docs/widgets.md:3251 say the collapsed row runs activate().

Requested by Antonio 2026-11-18.

THE ESTABLISHED FORM (docs/widgets.md:3090, :1176; heca-grid-ui/src/event/handlers.rs:47-65): a widget acts with `.on_click(|ev| ev.dispatch(Intent::new("name").arg(..)))` (native) or `.on_press(Intent::new(..))` (described). The Intent (heca-view: a name plus args) goes to the sink the host installs (`install_intent_sink`, heca-grid-ui/src/intent.rs:24) and through the normal action door (permissions, confirmations). `move` only when the closure captures an outside value. The widget knows nothing of heca's actions. `prefix+/` picks are automatic for anything with a click (docs/widgets.md:3130).

STEP 1 — FIX THE LIBRARY FIRST (found in T374, verified with temporary tests 2026-11-18). Today the established form does not work for buttons:
- Button and IconButton have their OWN `on_click(impl Fn())` (heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/button/builders.rs:199, icon_button.rs:127), separate from the generic EventExt::on_click(|ev|). With only the event form: Enter / `Component::activate()` / WidgetIntent::Activate send nothing; the ButtonGroup ⋮ overflow row runs the button's own click handle (button_group.rs:187, button/builders.rs:71) and does nothing; IconButton stops being focusable and a single click target. Mouse click and `prefix+/` still work. Goal: ONE click path — a button given `on_click(|ev| ev.dispatch(..))` keeps Enter, the ⋮ row, focus and single-target behaviour.
- A hint (`prefix+/` pick) can carry only a closure; `intent::dispatch` is pub(crate) (heca-grid-ui/src/intent.rs:29), so a pick cannot be named by an Intent and the host's policy filter (hide the letter when the action is refused — today done by action_tooltip setting hint.intent, heca/src/chrome/panes/pane_header/shortcuts.rs:172-176) cannot work through the established form. Goal: a pick that carries the same Intent as the click, so the picker can ask the policy.
- Dialog buttons send SubmitOverlay{overlay: Some(id)}: `overlay` is #[serde(skip)] (heca/src/input/action.rs:604-611) and the sink builds overlay: None = front-most modal (heca/src/input/build/chrome.rs:82-85); the sink always stamps MouseContent (heca/src/app/startup.rs:192-196) while the layer emitter stamps Surface(key). Resolved by plan point 3.

STEP 2 — THE SITES that send events by hand (grep on main 2026-11-18: `emit.fire(` / `proxy.send_event(AppEvent::ChromeIntent`):
- chrome/window/scene/mod.rs:98, :319 (sidebar toggle)
- chrome/panes/pane_header/build.rs:226, :239 (header buttons; focus-first for zoom/float — zoom has zoom_column_at_index{ws_idx,col_idx} (actions/builtins/layout.rs:173); float has no pane-targeted form (pane.rs:45); focus_pane{pane_id} exists (navigation.rs:100))
- chrome/surfaces/overlay/modal.rs (dialog buttons)
- chrome/panes/pane/mod.rs:111; chrome/panes/terminal/mod.rs:169, :188; chrome/panes/column/mod.rs:43
- providers/workspaces/pane_row.rs:211, :216; providers/workspaces/workspace_frame.rs:71
- chrome/surfaces/expose/wiring.rs:42, :59, :65, :75
- chrome/surfaces/overlay/spec.rs:25, :41
- chrome/surfaces/palette/mod.rs:273; chrome/surfaces/palette/sessions.rs:120
- chrome/panes/workspace/seat.rs:79 (drag resize; found by the audit)
- app/startup.rs:193 (not a widget — the sink itself)
Header builtins map to catalog names: add_pane_to_column{ws_idx,col_idx}, move_pane_left/right{pane_id}, close_pane_by_id{pane_id}, zoom_column, float (T374 audit).

FOR EACH SITE: what it sends and whether it can be written as ev.dispatch(Intent). Report the ones that cannot, with the reason, before changing them; fix centrally, never per site. Convert the rest, delete hand-sending code and unused emitter plumbing. Tests per surface: a click (and Enter, and the ⋮ row where relevant) produces the expected Intent at the sink. Update docs/widgets.md if the catalog changes.

acceptedDecisions.title: Function events take a callback
acceptedDecisions.decision: on_click, on_right_click, on_double_click, on_middle_click, on_key_down, on_toggle and the other function events take a callback, as today. The shape on_click(callback | Intent) is dropped.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Rust cannot infer a closure's parameter type when the builder takes a trait that both closures and Intent implement: every existing .on_click(|ev| ..) would need a written type. Confirmed by Antonio, 2026-11-22.

acceptedDecisions.title: on_press(Intent) is the action builder
acceptedDecisions.decision: on_press(Intent) runs the same intent on a left click, on Enter/Space on the control holding the keyboard (through the activate action), and on the widget's prefix+/ letter. The letter carries the intent, so the picker hides it when the action is refused.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: One builder for "this control does this action", reachable by mouse, keyboard and hint letter alike. Confirmed by Antonio, 2026-11-22.

acceptedDecisions.title: Described nodes keep `press`
acceptedDecisions.decision: In described nodes, `press` keeps the meaning of on_press. The `click` event added on feat/t565-rest is removed; the other native names added there stay: double_click, right_click, middle_click, pointer_enter/leave, focus_gained/lost, key, scroll and the drag events.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Plugins describe the same action the native builder runs, under the same name. Confirmed by Antonio, 2026-11-22.

acceptedDecisions.title: Value-carrying events: not decided
acceptedDecisions.decision: Whether value-carrying events (DockFrame on_toggle, CardGrid on_activate/on_move, ToastStack on_dismiss/on_action, ScrollBar on_change) take an action is not decided. Nobody touches them until it is.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: How the value's argument is named is still open. Confirmed by Antonio, 2026-11-22.
